ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure gives four candidate control circuits A, B, C, and D. In A, the SB start button is on the left, the KM coil is on the right, and there is another contact labeled KM in the same series path as SB and the coil, with no bypass branch formed. In B, SB is on the upper main path, the KM coil is on the right, and below there is an auxiliary contact branch labeled KM, but its arrangement and connection points do not form a suitable self-holding power-supply path. In C, SB is located on the main path leading to the KM coil on the right, and at the same time below there is an auxiliary contact branch labeled KM connected across the two ends of SB, forming a bypass in parallel with SB. In D, SB, one KM contact, and the KM coil on the right are basically connected in series in the same path, with no correct parallel self-locking branch formed. Reasoning: The correct connection method for contactor self-holding control is: after SB is pressed, the KM coil is energized, and the normally open auxiliary contact of KM closes; this KM auxiliary contact must be in parallel with the start button SB, so that after SB is released, current can still reach the KM coil through the KM auxiliary contact, realizing self-holding. The KM contact in A is only in series and cannot hold; the positions of the auxiliary contacts in B and D cannot constitute a correct blocking/self-holding path; in C, SB is responsible for starting the KM coil, and the KM auxiliary contact is connected in parallel across SB, so it can maintain coil power supply after KM operates. Therefore the correct one is Figure C.

raw_record.question_text: Which figure shows the correct control circuit for the circuit shown in the image?

method.method_draft: First describe the visual structure of each candidate circuit: locate SB, the KM coil, and any auxiliary KM contact branches. Then apply the self-holding contactor rule: the auxiliary KM contact must be wired in parallel with the start pushbutton so that after SB is pressed and KM energizes, the KM contact maintains power to the coil. Reject A because its KM contact is merely in series and cannot provide holding; reject B and D because the auxiliary/contact placement does not form the correct seal-in path to the coil. Select the option whose topology has SB starting the coil and KM sealing around SB, which is Figure C.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中给出四个候选控制电路 A、B、C、D。A 中，SB 起动按钮在左侧，KM 线圈在右侧，另有一个标注 KM 的触点与 SB、线圈处在同一串联通路上，没有形成旁路支路。B 中，SB 在上方主通路，KM 线圈在右侧，下方有一个标注 KM 的辅助触点支路，但其布置与连接点没有形成合适的自保持供电路径。C 中，SB 位于通向右侧 KM 线圈的主通路上，同时下方有一个标注 KM 的辅助触点支路跨接在 SB 两端，形成与 SB 并联的旁路。D 中，SB 与一个 KM 触点及右侧 KM 线圈基本串接在同一路径中，没有形成正确的并联自锁支路。
推理：接触器自保持控制的正确接法是：按下 SB 后 KM 线圈得电，KM 的常开辅助触点闭合；该 KM 辅助触点必须与起动按钮 SB 并联，这样松开 SB 后电流仍能经 KM 辅助触点到达 KM 线圈，实现自保持。A 的 KM 触点只是串联，不能保持；B 和 D 的辅助触点位置不能构成正确的封锁/自保持通路；C 中 SB 负责起动 KM 线圈，KM 辅助触点并联跨接 SB，能在 KM 动作后维持线圈供电。因此正确的是 Figure C。

With the provided choices, it yields a single clear answer rather than multiple independent solution paths.
planner_metadata.image_role: Inspect the four labeled options A, B, C, and D. Note the positions of the SB pushbutton contact, the KM coil at the right, and the auxiliary KM contacts. In particular, option C shows the SB contact in the main control path to the KM coil and a KM auxiliary contact on a lower branch connected as a holding/seal-in path between the supply side and the node after the pushbutton; the other options either place KM only in series, put the bypass at the wrong nodes, or interrupt the coil path incorrectly.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question text only to know that the task is to choose which of the four labeled figures is the correct control circuit; no numerical data or extra textual conditions are needed.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use the standard contactor control rule: for a momentary start pushbutton controlling a KM coil, the correct control circuit must energize the coil through SB initially and then use a normally-open KM auxiliary contact in parallel with the start button as a self-locking/holding contact, without shorting the supply or bypassing the required series path incorrectly.
